topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and connecting the session to previous practical work on cancer histopathology.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to laboratory assays for testing the transforming properties of mutated genes.

topics.label: Functional classification and allele dynamics of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified functionally and how allele dosage and mutation types govern the phenotypes of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Forms, molecular mechanisms, and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how distinct defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells and trigger downstream cellular stress responses.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary predispositions, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how the sequential accumulation of somatic or inherited genetic alterations drives tumor development and ongoing cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with recommended reading and an outlook on the next session.
